title: Core: Fix error reporting in ManagerErrorBoundary
body:
## What I did

Restores the (unhandled) error reporting which broke due to the introduction of the React error boundary.

comments.label_reasoning: The comment identifies two correctness bugs: side effects running in render phase (causing double-invocation issues in Strict Mode) and an unstable component reference causing premature cleanup. Both are logic/correctness issues in how React rendering and component identity work.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment identifies two concrete correctness risks (render-phase side effects and unstable component reference) and provides a specific diff/fix to move RestoreGlobals outside the decorator and setup into useEffect.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

```shell

```

```shell
cat code/core/src/manager/components/error-boundary/ManagerErrorBoundary.tsx
```

Repository: storybookjs/storybook

Length of output: 6026

---



</details>

**Play function assertions are thorough and well-structured.**

Good coverage: DOM state, console output shape, and telemetry call count + payload. The `expect.any(Error)` / `expect.any(String)` matchers keep assertions resilient to irrelevant changes.

However, the assertions confirm that `ManagerErrorBoundary.tsx` calls `console.error()` directly at lines 168-169. Per coding guidelines, client-side logging must use `logger` from `storybook/internal/client-logger` instead of `console` methods. Update the production component to use the logger import.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In
`@code/core/src/manager/components/error-boundary/ManagerErrorBoundary.stories.tsx`
around lines 106 - 125, The component ManagerErrorBoundary is calling
console.error directly (observed in ManagerErrorBoundary.tsx) which violates
client-side logging policy; replace those console.error calls with the shared
logger from 'storybook/internal/client-logger' by importing logger (or the
appropriate named export) and invoking logger.error with the same message and
error/stack arguments, and remove or replace any console.* usages in the
component (e.g., the two calls currently emitting 'Storybook Manager UI Error:'
and 'Component Stack:') so tests still receive the same values but production
logging uses the imported logger.
```

</details>
